note: From midday until dark. Colombians often shorten all three greetings to just buenas.

sent.en: Good afternoon, how are you?

note: For arriving after dark as well as for going to bed.

sent.en: Good night, sleep well.

note: Informal. To someone you call usted: ¿cómo está?

sent.en: Hi Ana, how are you?

note: The standard reply on being introduced. The answer is igualmente.

sent.en: Nice to meet you, my name is Daniel.

note: A woman says encantada.

sent.en: Pleased to meet you.

note: Literally how do you call yourself? Polite form: ¿cómo se llama?

sent.en: Hi, what is your name?

note: Polite form: ¿de dónde es usted?

sent.en: And you, where are you from?

note: Literally we see each other. nos vemos mañana, see you tomorrow.

sent.en: Right, see you on Monday.

note: The everyday Colombian goodbye, often doubled: chao, chao.

sent.en: Bye, have a good one.

note: Said as someone leaves. The reply is igualmente.

sent.es: Gracias por todo, {que te vaya bien}.
sent.en: Thanks for everything, all the best.

note: To usted: cuídese.

sent.en: Right, take good care of yourself.

note: The Colombian reply to gracias, more than de nada.

sent.es: Gracias por la ayuda. {Con mucho gusto}.
sent.en: Thanks for the help. My pleasure.

note: What Colombian shopkeepers call out, and how they answer gracias.

sent.en: Can I help you? What do you need?

note: Colombian. Literally will you give me as a present, but it means could I have, and you still pay.

sent.en: Could I have a coffee, please?

note: The answer: son las tres, or es la una.

sent.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

note: Means the same as ¿cuánto cuesta?, and in Colombia is said at least as often.

sent.en: How much is this hat?

note: Nobody brings it until you ask.

sent.en: Excuse me, the bill, please.

note: Ask for el baño, never for a toilet by any other name.

sent.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

note: Say it early and often; it is a sentence that buys you time.

sent.en: Sorry, I do not understand.

note: Informal: ¿puedes repetir?

sent.en: Sorry, could you repeat that?

note: The other sentence that buys you time.

sent.en: More slowly, please, I am learning.

note: To a friend: ¿hablas inglés?

sent.en: Excuse me, do you speak English?

note: sé, with an accent, is I know. se without one is a pronoun.

sent.en: I do not know where it is.

note: The reply to an apology.

sent.en: Do not worry, it is fine.
Of course, no problem.

note: estar de acuerdo, to agree.

sent.en: I agree with you.

note: A warmer yes than plain sí.

sent.en: Will you help me? Of course.

note: The Colombian apology for anything small: qué pena con usted. Not what a shame, which is qué lástima.

sent.en: Sorry, I got the wrong door.

note: For real regret, or bad news. For bumping into someone, perdón.

sent.en: I am very sorry.

note: To get attention politely. To a friend: disculpa.

sent.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

note: Said to people eating, even strangers as you pass their table.

sent.en: Lunch is served. Enjoy your meal!
Happy birthday, Ana!

note: The Colombian form. Spain says felicidades.

sent.en: Congratulations on the new job!

note: Far milder than the English, and heard from everyone.

sent.en: My goodness, it is hot!

note: The shout for help in an emergency.

sent.en: He shouted: help!

note: Literally they robbed me. Report it at a police station, a CAI in Colombia.

sent.en: My phone has been stolen.

note: A woman says estoy perdida.

sent.en: Excuse me, I am lost.

sent.es: {Me siento mal}, me voy a la casa.
sent.en: I do not feel well, I am going home.

note: Colombians also say voy de afán.

sent.en: Sorry, I am in a hurry.

note: tener que, to have to.

sent.en: It is late, I have to go.

note: Weather uses hacer. A person who is hot says tengo calor.

sent.en: In Cartagena it is always hot.

note: tengo frío, I am cold.

sent.es: En Bogotá {hace frío} por la noche.
sent.en: In Bogotá it is cold at night.

note: tiempo is the weather here. Colombians also say hace buen clima.

sent.es: Hoy {hace buen tiempo}, vamos al parque.
sent.en: The weather is nice today, let us go to the park.

note: What is happening, or what is the matter with you.

sent.en: What is wrong? You look sad.

note: Colombian, from qué hubo. Casual, for friends.

sent.en: What is up, mate?

note: Colombian. Not what else? but how are things? The answer is bien, ¿y tú?

sent.en: Hi Juan, how is it going?

note: As a question, ¿todo bien?, it is a greeting.

sent.en: Do not worry, everything is fine.
They gave you the job? Great!

note: For food, and for anything pleasant: qué rico este clima.

sent.en: This juice is delicious!

en: it is all the same to me
note: Neutral, not rude. Colombians also say me da lo mismo.

sent.en: Pizza or pasta? I do not mind.

note: Followed by a verb or a noun: tengo ganas de dormir.

sent.en: I feel like eating something sweet.

note: From irse: let us leave. Colombians also say ¡vamos!

sent.en: It is late, let us go!

note: Said when called, and also when you have not left yet.

sent.en: Coming! Wait for me.

note: un momentico is the Colombian version, and longer than it sounds.

sent.en: Just a moment, please.
I will do it right now.

note: Colombian and slippery: it can mean right now or some time later. Ask ¿ahorita ya?

sent.en: I will call you in a bit.
At last we have arrived.

note: Also at the end: al final de la calle.

sent.en: In the end we did not go.

note: As a question, ¿en serio? is really?

sent.en: Seriously? I do not believe you.
By the way, did you talk to Ana?

note: A filler as common as like in English.

sent.en: It is expensive, I mean, really expensive.

sent.es: Me gustan las frutas, {por ejemplo} el mango.
sent.en: I like fruit, for example mango.

note: Also the honest answer to ¿cómo estás?

sent.en: I speak Spanish more or less.
Little by little I am understanding more.

note: Two words. sobretodo, written as one, is an overcoat.

sent.es: Me gusta la fruta, {sobre todo} el mango.
sent.en: I like fruit, especially mango.

note: As a question, ¿de verdad? is really?

sent.en: Honestly, it was not my fault.

note: The question that gets the rest of your vocabulary. ¿cómo se dice window en español?

sent.en: How do you say this in Spanish?

note: For your job. Polite form: ¿a qué se dedica?

sent.en: And what do you do?

note: Age is had, not been: tengo veinticinco años.

sent.en: Sorry, how old are you?

note: Says why you are slow, and usually gets people to slow down.

sent.en: Sorry, I am learning Spanish.
I only speak a little Spanish.

note: Agrees with whoever is welcomed: bienvenida, bienvenidos.

sent.en: Welcome to Colombia.
Thanks for everything, and have a good trip!

note: The Colombian good night.

sent.en: Good night, sleep well.
I am off to bed, see you tomorrow.

note: Informal: ¿me puedes ayudar?

sent.en: Excuse me, can you help me?

note: For places, Colombians say queda rather than está: ¿dónde queda el banco?

sent.en: Where is the museum?

note: derecho is straight on; a la derecha is right. Easy to mishear.

sent.en: Keep going straight on for two blocks.

note: To a taxi or bus driver.

sent.en: Excuse me, can you drop me here?

note: Colombian demorarse, to take time.

sent.es: {¿Cuánto se demora} el bus al centro?
sent.en: How long does the bus take to the centre?

note: To eat in is para comer aquí.

sent.en: A coffee to take away, please.

note: The fastest way to find the best dish.

sent.es: No sé qué pedir, {¿qué me recomienda?}
sent.en: I do not know what to order, what do you recommend?

note: Colombian. Literally what laziness.

sent.en: Washing the dishes, I cannot be bothered!

note: Colombian. pilas means batteries: stay switched on.

sent.es: {¡Pilas} con el celular en el bus!
sent.en: Watch your phone on the bus!

note: Colombian. As a reply, it is a keen yes.

sent.en: Shall we go to the beach? Sure.
At eight? Sounds good to me.

note: Polite form: ¿qué opina?

sent.en: What do you think of the idea?
Is it going to rain? I think so.
Is it open? I do not think so.

note: Encouragement, before a hard thing or after one.

sent.en: Come on, you are nearly finished!

note: For a pity. For an apology, Colombians say qué pena.

sent.en: They have already closed, what a shame!

note: Not dismissive, as whatever can be in English: any of them will do.

sent.en: Order whatever you like, it is on me.

note: Polite form: no se preocupe.

sent.en: Do not worry, I will sort it out.
